label: Mark van Roojen, Moral Cognitivism vs §3.5…: Stevenson's disagreement in attitude: when one person…
locator: §3.5, 'Stevenson (1944) begins his book by distinguishing the kind of disagreement in play when two people disagree in their ordinary beliefs from “disagreements in attitude” which involve conative clash.'
interpretation: Stevenson distinguishes disagreement in belief from 'disagreements in attitude', a conative clash, holds that moral disagreements involve both, and uses this to motivate his emotivism. Read as the emotivist's replacement answer to Q-MORAL-DISAGREEMENT: the distinctively moral part of a disagreement is a clash of attitudes, not a contradiction. Attribution reading on a secondary witness: the claim records the position the entry reports, not a thesis of the entry's author. This remains a secondary-witness reading of the 1944 position. A distinct primary 1937 refinement is now pinned in STEVENSON-1937-27-29-INTEREST-DISAGREEMENT; the primary account does not retroactively change this claim’s witness.
